good.persian-carpet.desc: Hand-knotted carpets from the looms of Isfahan, Tabriz, and Kerman. The finest have a thousand knots to the square inch; their colours deepen with age.
good.persian-carpet.name: Persian Carpet
good.porcelain.desc: The white clay of Jingdezhen, fired at a heat that would melt iron, glazed with cobalt blue from Persia. So thin that light passes through; so hard that steel cannot scratch it.
good.porcelain.name: Porcelain
good.rhubarb.desc: The root of the medicinal rhubarb plant, grown in the mountains of Tangut and Cathay. More valuable than many spices; cures fevers and purges the body.
good.rhubarb.name: Rhubarb
good.rosewater.desc: Water distilled from the petals of Damask roses, grown in the gardens of Persia. Used in cooking, perfume, and the washing of honoured guests' hands.
good.rosewater.name: Rosewater
good.sable.desc: The sable of the Siberian forest — the most valuable fur in the world. The Kaan's winter robes are lined with it; a single pelt buys a horse.
good.sable.name: Sable
good.salt.desc: Salt from the mines of the Punjab, the pans of the Sahara, and the shores of the Black Sea. Salt is money on the steppe — a cake of salt buys a sheep.
good.salt.name: Salt
good.sandalwood.desc: The fragrant heartwood of the sandal tree, grown in the hills of southern India and the islands of Indonesia. Carved into boxes, burned as incense, or distilled into oil.
good.sandalwood.name: Sandalwood
good.silk.desc: The queen of fabrics — thread spun by the silkworm from the leaves of the mulberry, dyed with saffron, indigo, madder, and cochineal. A bolt of the finest silk sells for its weight in silver.
good.silk.name: Silk
good.silverware.desc: Silver plates, cups, and candlesticks from the workshops of Nuremberg and Limoges. The Latins' finest export to the East.
good.silverware.name: Silverware
good.steppe-horse.desc: The horses of the Mongol steppe — small, shaggy, and tireless. They can survive on grass buried under snow and carry a rider two hundred miles in a day.
good.steppe-horse.name: Steppe Horse
good.sugar.desc: Cane sugar from the plantations of the Levant and the islands of the Indian Ocean. Once a medicine, now the sweetener of kings and merchants.
good.sugar.name: Sugar
good.tabriz-pearls.desc: Pearls from the oyster beds of the Persian Gulf, sorted and drilled in the bazaars of Tabriz. A matched string of fifty pearls is worth a ship.
good.tabriz-pearls.name: Tabriz Pearls
good.tea.desc: The leaf of the Camellia bush, picked in spring, dried in the sun, pressed into bricks for the caravan trade. The Kaan's court drinks tea with milk and salt; the south drinks it clear.
good.tea.name: Tea
good.tin.desc: Tin from the mines of the Malay Peninsula, smelted into ingots and shipped to China and India. Mixed with copper, it makes bronze — the metal of bells, cannon, and Buddhas.
good.tin.name: Tin
good.tortoiseshell.desc: The mottled brown shell of the hawksbill turtle, harvested in the islands of the Indian Ocean. Heated and pressed into combs, boxes, and the inlay of fine furniture.
good.tortoiseshell.name: Tortoiseshell
good.turmeric.desc: The golden root of the turmeric plant, dried and ground into a powder that dyes cloth, flavours food, and heals wounds. The colour of a monk's robe.
good.turmeric.name: Turmeric
good.turquoise.desc: Sky-blue turquoise from the mines of Nishapur in Persia. Set in silver and worn as protection against the evil eye and falls from horseback.
good.turquoise.name: Turquoise
good.woolen-cloth.desc: Heavy woolen cloth from the Flemish looms, dyed with madder, woad, and weld. The best is as smooth as silk and as warm as a camel's coat.
good.woolen-cloth.name: Woollen Cloth

market.zayton.item.cinnabar: Cinnabar from the mountain mines of the south, sold in both the raw stone and the ground powder — the latter in small stoppered bottles because the wind off the haven will carry it away by the grain.
market.zayton.item.dehua-porcelain: Blanc de Chine out of the Dehua kilns — unglazed on the surface, warm as ivory. The Arab merchants call it 'the fat of the earth' and pay the forty-four in the hundred freight without complaint.
market.zayton.item.ginger: Preserved ginger in clay jars sealed with wax, bound for the galleys of Hormuz and Aden. The spice merchants say a ship without ginger is a ship that will lose half its crew to the flux.
market.zayton.item.hangzhou-fan: Folding fans from Kinsay, their ribs of sandalwood, their leaves painted with calligraphy. A merchant who buys a crate of these at Zayton can sell them in Damascus for ten times the price.
market.zayton.item.lacquerware: Black and cinnabar-red lacquer from the workshops of Fuju, cured in the damp heat of the coastal summer. The Indian merchants prize it for the way candlelight moves across the surface like oil on dark water.
market.zayton.item.musk: The musk-pod from the deer of the Tibetan marches, brought down to Zayton by caravan through the passes. A single pod, no bigger than a walnut, will scent a cargo of silk for a month.
market.zayton.item.paper-money: The Kaan's own currency, printed on mulberry-bark sheets with the imperial seal in vermilion. The quay-side money-changers will swap silver for paper at a rate that changes with the tide.
market.zayton.item.porcelain: The white ware of Jingdezhen, packed in straw and sawdust, carried down the rivers on flat-bottomed boats. A percentage of every crate is broken in transit, and the merchants have already figured that cost into the price you pay.
market.zayton.item.rhubarb: The dried root of the Tangut rhubarb — worth more pound for pound than cinnamon in the apothecaries of Venice. The warehousemen weigh it on the same brass scales they use for pearls.
market.zayton.item.silk: Bales of raw Manzi silk, stacked eight-high in the customs shed, waiting to be weighed and taxed. The Kaan's clerks nick a corner of every bale to check the grade; finer than any the Persians spin.
market.zayton.item.sugar: Cane sugar from the plantations of Fuju, shipped up the coast in cone-shaped loaves wrapped in palm-leaf. A cone of sugar is the universal gift at the quay; no deal is closed without one.
market.zayton.item.tea: Tea pressed into bricks and stamped with the producer's chop. The quayside merchants will trade a brick for a sack of pepper straight across, and both sides consider it a bargain.
npc.npc-zayton-mentor.name: The Woman Who Reads the Slips
npc.npc-zayton-mentor.omen: She has read slips for forty years, and remembers every master who ignored one.
retainer.cambaluc-mentor.fate_0: This year, a former student now high in the Kaan's service will offer him a pardon. Accepting means returning to Cambaluc — the one city he has sworn never to enter again.
retainer.cambaluc-mentor.fate_1: The scholar's eyes are failing. By the end of the year, he will need a scribe to read him the oracle books.
retainer.cambaluc-mentor.name: Scholar Wang of the Hanlin
retainer.cambaluc-mentor.origin: A Hanlin academician who fell from favour at the Kaan's court after disputing the interpretation of an oracle. He now teaches the I Ching to anyone who will listen.
retainer.cambaluc-mentor.quest: Wang believes that the true text of the I Ching was lost when the Qin emperor burned the books, and that a fragment survives in a monastery in the Tangut mountains. He seeks a travelling companion to help him find it.
retainer.cambaluc-mentor.sign: His fingernails are stained black from years of grinding ink. He has not written a single character since the day he left the court.
retainer.camel-driver.fate_0: This year, Bekter will attempt his forty-first crossing. The desert is a jealous wife, he says; she does not like to let a man go.
retainer.camel-driver.fate_1: One of Bekter's camels has developed a strange white patch on its flank. The old man believes it is a mark of blessing, but the other drivers call it a curse.
retainer.camel-driver.name: Old Bekter
retainer.camel-driver.origin: A Bactrian camel-driver who has crossed the Great Desert forty times. He has more miles on his knees than most men have in their whole bodies. He speaks to his camels in a language only they understand.
retainer.camel-driver.quest: Bekter once buried a hoard of silver at a place in the desert whose location he can only find by the stars. He wants to retrieve it before he dies. He will need help carrying it out.
retainer.camel-driver.sign: He can taste the water in the air. When he says a well is dry, every man in the caravan believes him — he has never been wrong.
retainer.cotanese-weaver.fate_0: A carpet Gulbibi wove ten years ago has been recognised by a merchant in Cambaluc as the work of a 'master of Khotan.' Buyers are searching for her. Fame will find her this year — whether she wants it or not.
retainer.cotanese-weaver.fate_1: The indigo crop failed this year. Her blue thread is running out, and without it, her carpets cannot be sold as the finest grade.
retainer.cotanese-weaver.name: Gulbibi the Weaver
retainer.cotanese-weaver.origin: A master carpet-weaver from Khotan, who can draw from memory the pattern of any carpet she has seen for more than five minutes. Her hands are stained with madder, indigo, and walnut.
retainer.cotanese-weaver.quest: Gulbibi's mother taught her a pattern that no other weaver in Khotan knows — a prayer for safe journey encoded in knot-counts and colour sequences. She wants to weave one last copy of it before her eyes fail.
retainer.cotanese-weaver.sign: She ties one knot in every carpet wrong, deliberately. 'Only God makes things perfect,' she says.
retainer.guard-aleppo.fate_0: A scar on his shoulder aches before storms. This year, it will ache for three weeks straight — and the storm that follows will change everything.
retainer.guard-aleppo.fate_1: An old comrade from the Mamluk corps has become a bandit chief in the mountains of Anatolia. Yusuf will have to choose: join him, turn him in, or pretend he never heard the name.
retainer.guard-aleppo.name: Yusuf the Circassian
retainer.guard-aleppo.origin: A former Mamluk slave-soldier who bought his freedom in the markets of Aleppo. He fought in the Sultan's cavalry against the Franks and the Mongols.
retainer.guard-aleppo.quest: Yusuf seeks the man who taught him to fight — an old weapons-master who retired to a monastery in the Caucasus. He wants to return the broken sword and receive a new one.
retainer.guard-aleppo.sign: He carries a sword with a broken tip. The break, he says, was a mercy; the man it broke against lived.
retainer.kinsay-mentor.fate_0: This year, a client whose fortune she once read will return — not for another reading, but for her. He has been looking for twenty years.
retainer.kinsay-mentor.fate_1: Lin's chart shows a clash between her fire and the year's water. The southern sea roads are dangerous for her this year; the northern roads, however, will bring an unexpected inheritance.
retainer.kinsay-mentor.name: Lin Sanniang
retainer.kinsay-mentor.origin: A fortune-teller from the pleasure quarters of Kinsay, who read a hundred faces a day and never forgot one. She learned the Four Pillars from an old astrologer who took her in as a girl.
retainer.kinsay-mentor.quest: Lin's mentor died leaving a sealed box that can only be opened on the day her chart predicts. She carries it everywhere but has never opened it. The predicted day falls this year — somewhere on the road.
retainer.kinsay-mentor.sign: She never reads her own chart. 'The gods do not need to know I am watching back,' she says.
retainer.mazu-priestess.fate_0: A ship blessed by A-Mei three years ago has been sighted off the coast of Champa. Everyone aboard was given up for dead. Their return will be either a miracle or a scandal.
retainer.mazu-priestess.fate_1: The temple of Mazu needs a new roof. A-Mei must raise the funds this year, or the spring rains will ruin the goddess's image.
retainer.mazu-priestess.name: A-Mei of the Sea
retainer.mazu-priestess.origin: A priestess of Mazu at the great temple in Zayton. She has blessed a thousand ships and watched a hundred of them fail to return. Her eyes are old with the sea.
retainer.mazu-priestess.quest: A-Mei believes that Mazu's power is fading because the source of her blessing — a sacred spring on the island of Meizhou — has been polluted by a shipwreck. She seeks travellers to help her cleanse it.
retainer.mazu-priestess.sign: The incense she burns in the temple always drifts toward the sea, never toward the land. She says Mazu is calling.
retainer.nestorian-priest.fate_0: This year, Father Simeon will find what he has been looking for — but it will not be what he expected. The Prester John of legend is dead; only his descendants remain, ruling a small tribe in the Ordos.
retainer.nestorian-priest.fate_1: A Nestorian bishop in Cambaluc has accused Simeon of heresy. The road east may be closed to him this year.
retainer.nestorian-priest.name: Father Simeon
retainer.nestorian-priest.origin: A Nestorian priest from Mosul, travelling east in search of the Christian kingdom of Prester John. He has crossed the steppe twice and been turned back twice.
retainer.nestorian-priest.quest: Simeon believes that the Nestorian church in Cambaluc holds a Gospel written in the hand of St. Thomas himself. He wants to see it, touch it, and copy it before he dies.
retainer.nestorian-priest.sign: He carries a reliquary that contains, he says, a fragment of the True Cross. No one has ever seen him open it.
retainer.steppe-guide.fate_0: This year, a blizzard will test him as no blizzard has before. If he survives it, his confidence will carry the whole party.
retainer.steppe-guide.fate_1: Temur's clan will call him home this year for a marriage he cannot refuse. He may return — or he may not.
retainer.steppe-guide.name: Temur the Herder
retainer.steppe-guide.origin: A Mongol of the Keraite clan, raised on the steppe north of the Gobi. He can navigate by the stars, read the weather in the taste of the wind, and find water where no man sees any.
retainer.steppe-guide.quest: Temur's elder brother was taken by a rival clan in a raid ten years ago. He has heard a rumour that the man is alive, a slave in the markets of Samarcand. He will not ask for help, but his eyes search every face in every crowd.
retainer.steppe-guide.sign: He cannot enter a walled city without first circling its walls three times. An old steppe custom, he says.
retainer.tartar-messenger.fate_0: A message Altan is carrying this year contains news that will start a war. He does not know it yet — but if he reads it, he will have to decide whether to deliver it.
retainer.tartar-messenger.fate_1: The Kaan's post is expanding this year. A new station will open in a place where no messenger has gone before. Altan will be the first — or someone else will.
retainer.tartar-messenger.name: Altan the Arrow
retainer.tartar-messenger.origin: A Tartar courier of the Kaan's yam, the imperial post. He can ride two hundred miles in a day, changing horses at every station. He knows every post-house between Cambaluc and Samarcand.
retainer.tartar-messenger.quest: Altan's father was a courier who died carrying a message from the Kaan to the Ilkhan. The message was never delivered. Altan wants to find out what it said and whether it changed the course of a war.
retainer.tartar-messenger.sign: He never dismounts on the left side of a horse. The one time he did, the horse threw him and he broke three ribs.
retainer.tauris-merchant.fate_0: This year, a debt from his past will find him. Pay it or flee — either way, the road changes.
retainer.tauris-merchant.fate_1: Mirza's network of informants will bring word of a caravan that doubles its value by the time it reaches the sea.
retainer.tauris-merchant.name: Mirza of Tabriz
retainer.tauris-merchant.origin: A Persian merchant who once ran the Genoese fondaco in Tauris. He knows every language between Venice and Cambaluc, and the price of every goods.
retainer.tauris-merchant.quest: Mirza owes a sum of silver to a merchant-house in Hormuz. He will not speak of it, but he watches every ship that docks in every port. Help him settle the debt, and he will share his knowledge of the southern sea roads.
retainer.tauris-merchant.sign: He never sleeps with his back to a door. When asked why, he changes the subject.
retainer.venetian-clerk.fate_0: Pietro's gambling debt will catch up with him this year. A Venetian agent in Tauris has a warrant — or says he does.
retainer.venetian-clerk.fate_1: A merchant in Kinsay has noticed Pietro's handwriting and offered him a position keeping the books of a pepper fleet. The salary is a fortune; the temptation to embezzle is greater.
retainer.venetian-clerk.name: Pietro the Clerk
retainer.venetian-clerk.origin: A Venetian notary's apprentice who stowed away on a galley to escape a gambling debt. He has a beautiful hand for writing, a head for figures, and a complete inability to keep his mouth shut.
retainer.venetian-clerk.quest: Pietro wants to compose a book of his travels — a Merchants' Guide to the East, with prices, routes, and notes on every city. He needs to visit twelve more cities before he has enough material.
retainer.venetian-clerk.sign: He writes a letter to Venice every month and posts none of them. The stack in his saddlebag is a year thick.
retainer.zayton-mentor.fate_0: This year, the monsoon will arrive a week early. If he is at sea when it comes, his ship will outrun the storm. If he is in port, the harbour will be blocked for a month.
retainer.zayton-mentor.fate_1: A rival captain has challenged his monopoly on the Zayton-Hormuz route. Majid will need to prove his worth this year — or lose his ship.
retainer.zayton-mentor.name: Captain Majid of Zayton
retainer.zayton-mentor.origin: An Arab sea-captain who has made the voyage from Zayton to Hormuz thirty times. He knows every reef, every current, and every monsoon between the China Sea and the Persian Gulf.
retainer.zayton-mentor.quest: Twenty years ago, Majid lost a chest of pearls overboard in a storm off the coast of Champa. A diver recently claimed to have found it. Majid will detour a thousand miles on the rumour alone.
retainer.zayton-mentor.sign: He always consults the temple lots before setting sail. He has never ignored a lot in his life — and he has never been shipwrecked.
